review_notes: I read the whole file with the simp interface in mind. I checked the @[simp] lemmas: timeShift_*, boundaryInclusionAt_mk, lowerSection_val, upperSection_val, uStrip_val, vStrip_val, affineCircleArc_*, uPath_apply, vPath_apply, productCover_*, differenceCycle_val, arcSumCycle_val. Most look like ordinary unfolding or evaluation lemmas and show no clear loop or competing rule. The one concrete problem I found is in the monodromy-power and homologyNorm simp pair. I also confirmed that MappingTorusHomology.monodromyHomologyMap is an abbrev for singularHomologyMap (in FundamentalGroupVanKampen2.lean). I could not run Lean, so the claim that the two simp lemmas interact is based on reducible unfolding in the discrimination tree. It is not an observed simplifier behaviour. The finding is minor and fairly speculative.

homologyNorm m B n a =

findings.problem: Two @[simp] rules appear to compete over the same subterm. `monodromyHomologyMap_pow` is @[simp], and `monodromyHomologyMap` is an `abbrev` for `singularHomologyMap (f : C(X, X)) n`. The lemma's LHS is therefore keyed, after reducible unfolding, on `singularHomologyMap ((B ^ k : X ≃ₜ X) : C(X, X)) n`. That is exactly the shape `homologyNorm_apply` produces on its RHS. So the RHS of the simp lemma `homologyNorm_apply` is not simp-normal: a full `simp` would immediately rewrite each summand to `(singularHomologyMap B n) ^ k a`. The two forms are connected only by definitional unfolding, which is why `homologyNorm_eq_sum_powers` is closed by `exact monodromyHomologyMap_pow ..`. The power rule is also written with the `monodromyHomologyMap` head, which hides that it acts on every `singularHomologyMap` of a coerced power. The only current uses are `simp only` calls, so the mismatch has no effect now. Any full `simp` that uses `homologyNorm_apply` will land on a different normal form from the one the local coordinate lemmas state, such as `upperSection_homology_coordinates`.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form and state the rules consistently. For example, restate `homologyNorm_apply` as `∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, ((singularHomologyMap (B : C(X, X)) n) ^ k) a`, with the power form on the RHS. Equivalently, make `homologyNorm_eq_sum_powers` the unfolding lemma, and keep `homologyNorm_apply` non-simp or derive it from that form. Also state `monodromyHomologyMap_pow` with an explicit `singularHomologyMap` LHS, or drop its @[simp] attribute if it is only meant to be applied by `exact`.
findings.benefit: A full `simp` on `homologyNorm m B n a` would give one predictable normal form. That form would match the power-sum form already used in `homologyNorm_eq_sum_powers` and by its downstream users in Elliptic/Core7 and PeriodFamily/Core6. The `exact`-by-defeq bridge between the `abbrev` and its unfolding would also no longer be needed.
